title: Glowmere
summary: Two-thumb shooter in a pool of light reeds, where every enemy keeps the beat
description:
**Glowmere** is a fast shooter for two thumbs in a round pool of light. Its reeds sway with a slow current, lean away from every blast and lie down in your wake, and everything in the pool keeps time with the music. No ads, no account, no tracking.

**Playing**

- **Two thumbs, anywhere.** Put a thumb down on the left half of the screen and drag to fly. Drag on the right half to aim: your ship fires for as long as that thumb stays down. The sticks appear wherever you touch.
- **One-thumb mode** lets the ship aim and fire by itself, at the nearest enemy it can hurt, so you only steer.
- **Creatures that keep the beat.** Pouncers creep closer and leap on every second beat, fireflies swarm and blink in time, sowers fling a petal at you every few beats, shieldbacks turn their shields to meet your shots, and a warden's eye stays shut while its guards circle it. Lancers cross the pool dead straight and rebound off the shore. Watch the rhythm and you see the next move coming, even with the music off.
- **Eight sectors of six waves.** Each sector ends in a surge, and clearing it opens the next. The first five each bring in a new kind of enemy.
- **Endless mode** opens once you have cleared Sector 2: the waves keep coming and keep getting faster.
- **Hull and novas.** Your hull takes four hits, and every wave you clear mends a segment. A nova sweeps away every enemy it reaches; its charge fills as you destroy enemies, and you can hold three.
- **Score and multiplier.** Destroyed enemies leave sparks. Fly through them to warm the meter and raise the multiplier up to ×8, which also widens your fire from two streams to a five-way spread. The meter cools while enemies are about, so keep collecting.
- **Power-ups and upgrades.** Gold-ringed elites drop capsules with six power-ups: ricochet, piercing and homing shots, drones, time warp and a shield. After waves 1, 3 and 5 (every second wave in Endless) you pick one of three upgrades, such as side cannons, chain lightning or quicker nova charges, and they stack for the rest of the run.
- **A guide built in.** How to play explains the controls, the scoring, every power-up and upgrade, and each enemy.

**Your game and your scores**

- The run in progress is saved as you play, so you can close the app and continue where you left off. The game pauses itself when you leave it.
- After every run: your score, kills, top multiplier and time, and the best score for each sector and for Endless.
- Progress and settings stay on your phone. Erase progress starts the sectors over and keeps your settings.

**Sound and looks**

- Every sound is synthesised as you play, and the music is a live sequencer that builds up with each wave. Sound effects, music and volume each have their own setting.
- Glowing creatures over a pool of swaying light reeds: a warm night palette, or daylight on paper. Where a phone can't use the faster graphics, the game draws in a plainer style, and Auto quality lowers the resolution if the frame rate drops.
- The home screen is the pool itself: tap the water to send a gust through the reeds.
- Light and dark designs, or follow the phone. Reduce motion calms the reeds and removes screen shake, flashes and blinking; it follows your phone's setting unless you choose otherwise.
- With a keyboard and mouse: WASD to move, the arrow keys or the mouse to aim and fire, Space for a nova, P to pause. Waves, hits to the hull, novas and power-ups are announced to screen readers.
- In English or Slovak, following your phone's language.

**What it never does**

- No ads, no in-app purchases, no locked features.
- No account and no sign-in.
- No internet access: the game works offline and cannot connect anywhere.
- No analytics or tracking of any kind.
